patient_summary:
Hello there, you're in the hospital today. You had a small growth on your nose that needed to be taken out. The doctors are going to remove it and then close the area. You were given a special medicine to help you sleep during the procedure. After the surgery, you'll take some medicine to help you feel better.

You'll be given a few medicines to take after you leave the hospital:
- Minocycline
- Darvocet-N 100

You'll need to take these medicines for a few days. The doctors will check on you to make sure everything is healing well. If you have any pain or if you feel sick, you should tell the nurses or doctors right away.

The doctors used a special magnifying glass to help them during the surgery. They made sure all the edges of the cut were clean. They closed the area with a special stitch technique. You'll have some bandages on your nose for a few days, and you might feel some pressure.

If you have any questions or if you feel uncomfortable, you can always ask the nurses or doctors. They're there to help you. You'll be okay, and you'll be back to your normal self soon.
caregiver_checklist: Give the patient minocycline and Darvocet-N 100 as prescribed.
Check the patient's vital signs and overall condition hourly.
Watch for signs of infection such as increased redness, swelling, or pus.
Call the healthcare provider if the patient develops fever or signs of infection.
Schedule a follow-up appointment in 2 weeks for wound check.
Monitor for signs of anesthesia complications such as dizziness or confusion.
Call the healthcare provider if the patient experiences severe pain or unexpected symptoms.
Check the wound dressing for signs of infection or drainage.
Watch for signs of bleeding or excessive drainage.
Call the healthcare provider if the patient has any concerns or questions.

source_text: PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Basal cell carcinoma, nasal tip, previous positive biopsy.,POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Basal cell carcinoma, nasal tip, previous positive biopsy.,OPERATION PERFORMED: , Excision of nasal tip basal carcinoma.  Total area of excision, approximately 1 cm to 12 mm frozen section x2, final margins clear.,INDICATION: , A 66-year-old female for excision of nasal basal cell carcinoma.  This area is to be excised accordingly and closed.  We had multiple discussions regarding types of closure.,SUMMARY: , The patient was brought to the OR in satisfactory condition and placed supine on the OR table.  Underwent general anesthesia along with Marcaine in the nasal tip areas for planned excision.  The area was injected, after sterile prep and drape, with Marcaine 0.25% with 1:200,000 adrenaline.,The specimen was sent to pathology.  Margins were still positive at the inferior 6 o'clock ***** margin and this was resubmitted accordingly.  Final margins were clear.,Closure consisted of undermining circumferentially.  Advancement closure with dog ear removal distally and proximally was accomplished without difficulty.  Closure with interrupted 5-0 Monocryl running 7-0 nylon followed by Xeroform gauze, light pressure dressing, and Steri-Strips.,The patient is discharged on minocycline and Darvocet-N 100.,NOTE:,  The 2.6 mm loupe magnification was utilized throughout the procedure.  No complications noted with excellent and all clear margins at the termination.  An advancement closure technique was utilized.
